scenario.fault_family: link cut (both fabric uplinks of one leaf)
scenario.prompt_to_agent:
A user on pc_0_1 (10.0.1.2) reports a total outage: nothing across the
fabric responds, and pc_0_0 (10.0.0.2) cannot reach pc_0_1 either.
pc_0_1 CAN still ping its own gateway 10.0.1.1, and leaf_router_0_1
itself is up and reachable on its console -- its FRR daemons are all
running. Both of its BGP sessions to the spines are gone. Diagnose.

ip link set eth0 down
  ip link set eth1 down

post_inject_check.command: ip -br link show eth0 | grep -c UP
ip -br link show eth1 | grep -c UP

scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: leaf_router_0_1 eth0 and eth1 -- BOTH fabric
  uplinks: eth0 (172.16.0.7/31, link subnet 172.16.0.6/31) to
  spine_router_0_0 and eth1 (172.16.0.11/31, link subnet
  172.16.0.10/31) to spine_router_0_1
Mechanism: leaf_router_0_1's only paths into the CLOS fabric are its
  two spine uplinks. With both interfaces down, both BGP sessions drop
  and the leaf can neither learn 10.0.0.0/24 nor deliver its own
  10.0.1.0/24 traffic anywhere -- the CLOS redundancy is defeated
  because BOTH members of the redundant pair are down. The host-facing
  port eth2 (10.0.1.1/24) is untouched, so pc_0_1 still reaches its
  gateway but nothing beyond it. Note this is the one link-fault shape
  where redundancy does not save the leaf; a single downed uplink
  would only degrade redundancy.
Localization: leaf_router_0_1
Root cause: both spine-facing interfaces (eth0, eth1) down on
  leaf_router_0_1
Fix: `ip link set eth0 up` and `ip link set eth1 up` on
  leaf_router_0_1; both BGP sessions re-establish on their own.
scenario.fix_spec:
`ip link set eth0 up && ip link set eth1 up` on leaf_router_0_1. Once
the uplinks are UP the sessions to both spines come back and pc_0_1
regains fabric reachability.
scoring_axes: must-identify-affected-links: BOTH spine uplinks down -- eth0 (to spine_router_0_0) AND eth1 (to spine_router_0_1)
must-distinguish-symptom-pattern: pc_0_1 still reaches its gateway (host link fine) but nothing past the leaf
bonus-notes-host-link-fine: explicitly rules out the host access link / pc_0_1 itself (eth2 UP, gateway pingable)

agent.diagnosis_text:
Both uplink interfaces on leaf_router_0_1 — eth0 (172.16.0.7/31, toward
spine_router_0_0) and eth1 (172.16.0.11/31, toward spine_router_0_1) —
have been brought down at the Linux kernel level. The interfaces carry the
flags <BROADCAST,MULTICAST> with no UP or LOWER_UP, meaning they were
explicitly shut down via `ip link set ethX down`, not by FRR (protodown is
off on both, and the running FRR configuration contains no shutdown
statements for those interfaces). FRR records Link ups: 0 (never) and a
single Link down event for each at the identical timestamp
2026/08/04 18:30:14.04, confirming a simultaneous, deliberate
administrative action. Because these are the only two uplinks connecting
the leaf to the spine layer, all L3 paths out of the leaf are severed: BGP
cannot establish TCP sessions to 172.16.0.6 or 172.16.0.10, so both eBGP
peers are stuck in Active. With no BGP routes installed, leaf_router_0_1's
RIB contains only the local 10.0.1.0/24 connected route, so any packet
from pc_0_1 destined outside its own subnet is returned with "Destination
Net Unreachable". pc_0_1 can still reach its gateway (eth2 is UP and
locally connected) but nothing beyond. The counterpart spine interfaces
(spine_router_0_0:eth2 and spine_router_0_1:eth2) are healthy and up.

Root cause: both kernel-level uplink interfaces (eth0, eth1) on
leaf_router_0_1 were administratively shut down simultaneously, severing
all BGP sessions and removing all fabric routes from that leaf.

Corrective fix: on leaf_router_0_1 run `ip link set eth0 up && ip link set
eth1 up`. The interfaces will re-acquire carrier (the spine sides are
already up), BGP sessions will re-establish, 10.0.1.0/24 will be
re-advertised into the fabric, and return routes will be learned, restoring
full pc_0_1 ↔ pc_0_0 connectivity. To make the fix persistent across
restarts, ensure the startup script does not issue any `ip link set down`
for these interfaces.
